skill.name: truth-layer
skill.description: Verifies engineering claims against real build, test, type, and repository evidence before reporting completion.
skill.summary: Validate project status claims before accepting completion.
skill.author: CleanExpo

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown code fences and inline examples, not executable Ruby or shell backticks. Two findings are confirmed because the skill instructs agents to run build or typecheck commands, which can execute project-defined scripts.

remediation.issue: Automatic build and typecheck command execution
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before Bash commands and show the exact command before execution. Prefer read-only checks when possible.

finding_verdicts.reason: This is a Markdown blocker-report template inside a fenced block. It does not invoke shell, interpolate user input, or instruct Ruby backtick execution.
The evidence is Markdown fence syntax around documentation. No executable command or dynamic command construction is present in this span.
This is a TypeScript interface example in a Markdown code block. It describes result shape and does not execute a shell command.

The surrounding Step 2 instructions tell the agent to run actual build commands and typecheck commands. These can trigger project-defined scripts, so external command execution is intended even though the use is legitimate.
The inline `npm run typecheck` instruction is a concrete external command. NPM scripts are project-defined and can execute arbitrary local code, so this should require normal command safeguards.
This span is a plain-text blocker report format inside a Markdown fence. It does not contain executable syntax or a command runner.
The static hit is caused by Markdown fence syntax near a workflow diagram. The content describes routing logic, not shell execution.
This is an ASCII workflow diagram in a Markdown fenced block. It contains no executable command, interpreter directive, or user-controlled input.
The Commands & MCP Usage section instructs automatic Bash execution of build commands when blocked. That can run repository scripts, so it is a real external command requirement.
This is an example blocker report in a Markdown fence. It names a fix in prose but does not provide or execute a shell command.
The evidence is Markdown code-fence syntax after an example report. There is no command invocation or code execution path.
This fenced block shows an example false-positive status report. It is documentation text and does not execute shell commands.

content.value_statement: Teams lose time when status reports hide failing builds, stub tests, or unresolved blockers. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code verify claims before reporting completion.
actual_capabilities: Checks claimed progress against current repository evidence.
Requires build, type, and test verification before completion reports.
Identifies blockers with impact, root cause, current state, and next step.
Flags stub tests, hidden build errors, and unsupported readiness claims.
Provides structured blocker and verification report formats.
limitations: Depends on available repository, build, test, and tool access.
May need user approval before running local commands.
Does not replace human review for release decisions.
Can over-block when diagnostics are incomplete or stale.

use_cases.title: Review Release Readiness
use_cases.description: Verify build, test, and type status before a feature moves toward deployment.

use_cases.title: Audit AI Agent Claims
use_cases.description: Check whether an agent completion report matches the actual repository state.

use_cases.title: Surface Engineering Blockers
use_cases.description: Turn vague failures into clear blocker reports with impact and next actions.

prompt_templates.title: Check A Completion Claim
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner verification of a single claim.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use truth-layer to verify this completion claim against the current repo. Report blockers, evidence, confidence, and the next required action.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Build Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use truth-layer to audit build, typecheck, tests, and dependency state. Stop progress if any required check fails.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate Hidden Failures
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review after a suspicious success report.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use truth-layer to compare the claimed success with logs, test depth, file state, and known false-positive patterns.

prompt_templates.title: Gate Multi-Agent Work
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced orchestration before routing specialist agents.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use truth-layer as a preflight gate for this task. Decide whether work can proceed, route blockers, and document evidence.

output_examples.input: A feature is marked complete after a quick local check.
output_examples.output: Truth Layer reports that completion is not verified. The build result is missing, test depth is unclear, and type status needs confirmation.

output_examples.input: A deployment request depends on a claimed successful typecheck.
output_examples.output: Truth Layer asks for the actual typecheck result, records confidence, and blocks deployment until the evidence is available.

output_examples.input: A team needs a concise blocker report for a failed build.
output_examples.output: Truth Layer lists the failure, impact, root cause, current state, and the specific action needed to unblock work.

best_practices: Run verification before reporting completion or routing dependent work.
Record direct evidence for each claim, including failures and uncertainty.
Treat stub tests and missing logs as unresolved until proven otherwise.
anti_patterns: Marking work ready without a current build or typecheck result.
Counting empty test files as meaningful coverage.
Ignoring warnings that hide broken artifacts or incomplete verification.

faq.question: What does this skill verify?
faq.answer: It verifies engineering claims against build status, tests, type safety, file state, and blocker evidence.

faq.question: Does it run commands automatically?
faq.answer: It can guide command-based checks, but users should confirm local commands before execution.

faq.question: Who should use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when agents, developers, or release teams need evidence before accepting completion claims.

faq.question: Can it detect fake test coverage?
faq.answer: It looks for stub tests, shallow files, and unsupported coverage claims.

faq.question: Does it replace CI?
faq.answer: No. It helps interpret and demand evidence, but CI remains the source of automated enforcement.

faq.question: What happens when a blocker is found?
faq.answer: The skill stops dependent progress and reports the failure, impact, root cause, current state, and next action.
